News.title: This summer’s wildfire epidemic is one of the worst in decades – so why are deaths so low?
News.content:
Wildfires in Britain and Europe this year are among the worst in decades, yet direct deaths are at some of the lowest levels, according to a Telegraph analysis.

As of early August, 505,683 hectares of land have burned across Europe, forcing the evacuation of more than 360,000 people as uncontrollable flames reach major cities, towns, and villages.

The problem is global – in the US, Nevada declared a state of emergency over the weekend after a wildfire caused more than 42,000 people to evacuate their homes.

But what sets 2026 apart isn’t just the vast areas of land burned, but how few deaths have been caused by the fires.

This summer, just 14 people are reported to have died in European wildfires, the vast majority in a single blaze in Almería, southern Spain.

By comparison, more than 130 people were killed in the summer of 2017 – a toll driven largely by the Pedrógão Grande disaster in Portugal, where more than 60 people died on a single stretch of road.

In 2018, at least 100 others died in a single afternoon in the Mati disaster near Athens, despite total hectares burned that year being roughly a third of current levels.

Since the modern phenomenon of summer wildfires exploded in Europe a decade ago, the direct death toll has broadly trended downward, as the chart below shows.

News.title: Swine flu outbreak in Delhi swamps clinics and hospitals
News.content:
India is battling a surge in H1N1 flu infections, prompting the federal health ministry to step up surveillance and hospital preparedness.

The national capital New Delhi has recorded 1,777 cases this year, almost eight times the number (229) reported during the same period in 2025.

Dr Randeep Guleria, a senior pulmonologist and director of Medanta Medical School, Gurugram, says the H1N1 cases are much higher than reported.

“It’s quite likely that the reported numbers are an underestimate because they depend on how many people are tested,” Guleria said. “If you speak to patients admitted to hospital who test positive for H1N1, you often find that other members of their family have similar symptoms, although they have not been tested.”

“There is a surge and we are seeing a lot of patients. We are testing only those who come to hospital and are more seriously ill,” Guleria said.

H1N1, commonly known as swine flu, is a subtype of influenza A. It is a contagious respiratory infection that can cause fever and cough and in severe cases it can lead to pneumonia and respiratory failure.

Officials at the Indian Council of Medical Research said the rise did not mean the emergence of a new strain of the virus.

The surge comes during India’s rainy season, when seasonal influenza and other respiratory infections typically increase.

Doctors in Delhi say they are seeing more patients with high fevers, persistent coughs and flu-like symptoms, although most cases remain mild.

The H1N1 cases have been reported beyond New Delhi. The metro cities like Mumbai, Chennai and Bangaluru have reported a high number of cases, although the pattern is not uniform across the country.

Doctors in Bangaluru have reported more influenza A infections among children, with some developing pneumonia and respiratory distress.

India’s health minister JP Nadda said there was a need for continued vigilance and robust surveillance. He has asked officials to monitor unusual increases and clusters of cases and ensure hospitals could respond quickly.

“Swine flu (H1N1) can show up through symptoms such as fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches and fatigue… If you experience these symptoms, seek medical advice at your nearest healthcare centre,” the health ministry said on X.

Delhi’s health minister, Pankaj Kumar Singh, said the capital had enough beds, doctors, medicines and medical equipment to manage the increase. “Delhi is fully prepared to deal with the present health situation,” Singh said.

India has had several waves of H1N1 since the virus emerged globally in 2009.

The infection, commonly called swine flu, became a recurring seasonal respiratory illness after the 2009 pandemic rather than disappearing from circulation.

India recorded 3,320 H1N1 cases and 14 deaths in 2025, according to Ministry of Health data.

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.

Sports.title: Alvarez left with two options: Atletico or Arsenal
Sports.content:
Julian Alvarez must take one of two paths before the transfer deadline: stay at Atletico Madrid and try to rebuild his connection with the fans or get his head around a potential move to Arsenal.

Atletico have told him again that they will not sell him to Barcelona and that - coupled with the reaction of the club's supporters on Sunday - has left him "devastated", according to well-placed sources in Spain.

The situation is now "extremely tense", according to Atletico expert and journalist Ruben Uría.

"Neither Miguel Gil Marín (CEO of Atlético Madrid) nor the Apollo board want to sell the player to Barcelona," he told Sky Sports News. "The entire Apollo board supports Gil Marín's decision. Alvarez has been told."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Transfer Talk podcast, Sam Tighe and Daniel Storey debate whether Arsenal should gamble on signing Julian Alvarez despite the striker clearly wanting to sign for Barcelona

According to Uría, Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta has remained in contact with his former Atletico employers in recent days after Alvarez was booed off by supporters in the opening LaLiga game against Villarreal.

But Arsenal will need Alvarez to put Barcelona out of his mind and show he really wants to join Mikel Arteta's project before any serious negotiations or any offers can be made. In that vein, Arsenal are not currently hopeful of getting him in before September 1 and they are certainly not currently expecting it at the Emirates.

Alvarez still has his heart set on Barcelona. The question is, will this be the case as the transfer window comes to an end? Will the deadline have any effect? Arsenal will always be ready and open to Alvarez should he change his mind but, at the moment, any move looks very unlikely.

If Alvarez shifts his thinking before the end and pushes for an escape, Atletico are believed to be ready to listen to offers of around £130m (€150m) from Arsenal. Indeed, according to Uría, some people around the Argentine think it is increasingly impossible for him to stay at Atletico given the current atmosphere.

Should Arsenal complete a deal for Alvarez, it would be the 10th £100m+ signing in Premier League history.

Premier League £100m+ transfers Alexander Isak – £125m – Newcastle to Liverpool

Morgan Rogers – £117m - Aston Villa to Chelsea

Florian Wirtz – £116.5m – Bayer Leverkusen to Liverpool

Elliot Anderson – £116m – Nottingham Forest to Manchester City

Moises Caicedo – £115m – Brighton to Chelsea

Enzo Fernandez – £106.8m – Benfica to Chelsea

Declan Rice – £105m – West Ham to Arsenal

Sandro Tonali – £100m – Newcastle to Tottenham

Jack Grealish – £100m – Aston Villa to Manchester City

It would also be the fourth this summer, after Morgan Rogers' switch to Chelsea, Elliot Anderson's move to Manchester City and Sandro Tonali joining Tottenham.

Uría also told Sky Sports News: "Julian and his agent believe that everything that's happening is the fault of Gil Marín, Atletico Madrid's CEO, who publicly asked them to say they wanted to leave Atletico.

"For their part, Atletico Madrid argues that Julian already knew how Atletico played under Diego Simeone when he signed for the club, that he knew what contract he was signing and what its clause was, and they deny that Atletico told him he could leave for a direct rival.

"We are waiting to see how events unfold regarding Julian, waiting to see how Arsenal reacts, and if they have genuine interest in the Argentina player. Atletico Madrid will not sell to Barcelona.

"Our information today is that the Julian Alvarez situation has become very tense, and according to several reliable sources, right now, in this crucial week, there are only two paths: stay at Atletico Madrid to fulfil his contract or listen to Arsenal's offer and sign for the London club. Julian will have to make his decision."

Sports.title: Liverpool hold fresh Barcola talks with PSG
Sports.content:
Liverpool are holding further talks with Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday for Bradley Barcola.

There has been a gap in valuation between the two clubs throughout the summer, with PSG asking for around £145m for the France international.

However, the discussions that have taken place during this window have been described as positive, and there is optimism that a deal can be struck with a week left before the deadline.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Sam Blitz explains the four things Liverpool fans should know about transfer target Bradley Barcola

Sky Sports News understands there are good relations between the two clubs at the highest level. It is hoped this will help Liverpool and PSG reach an agreement.

Liverpool have also explored a move for Barcola's team-mate, Ibrahim Mbaye, who plays off the right wing.

The Premier League club's priority throughout this window has been to reinforce in wide areas.

They have been pursuing Barcola and Mbaye, while Brighton have also rejected two Liverpool offers for Yankuba Minteh, the latest being £60m.

Liverpool are currently the only club chasing Barcola, who has entered the final two years of his deal and has grown dissatisfied with his role at the European champions.

Liverpool, meanwhile, do not want to sell Cody Gakpo amid interest from Tottenham and Manchester City and would likely need two new wingers in before considering letting the Netherlands international go.

Sports.title: Forest agree club-record deal for Chelsea's Delap
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record £50m deal to sign Liam Delap from Chelsea.

The transfer is understood to be worth at least £45m, which could reach £50m with add-ons.

The striker is scheduled to have a medical on Wednesday.

Delap had interest from a number of other Premier League clubs, including Everton, but Forest have secured his signing.

Chelsea signed Delap last summer for £30m from Ipswich and valued him at around £50m this summer.

They could be set for a £20m profit on a striker who scored two goals in 41 appearances last season.

Forest's previous record transfer saw Omari Hutchison join for £37.5m from Ipswich Town in August 2025.

Image: Delap joined Chelsea last summer from Ipswich

Sherwood backs Forest's Delap move

Tim Sherwood speaking on Soccer Special:

"We know Liam's got the ability; he's shown that in the past. He needs to play on a regular basis now. He needs to stay fit.

"It never worked out at Chelsea. I never think he ever got a run in the team to give that striker the confidence; you need the manager to love you and play you every week, even if you're not playing well. I think he'll get that with Glasner - you've seen that with (Jean-Philippe Mateta) at Palace.

"He [Forest boss Oliver Glasner] likes to play with a big striker; he likes support. If he [Delap] can keep up with play, I think he'll score goals for Nottingham Forest, and I believe he will keep up with play.

"I think he's aggressive; he's got a lot of attributes to be a top, top striker, but Chelsea just did not work for him, and that's what happens.

"Forget about the price tag because the price tags all over the Premier League now are just ridiculous."

Forest are bringing in Delap to improve their striking options following Taiwo Awoniyi's £9m move to Coventry.

Oliver Glasner's side have been pursuing Tottenham midfielder Lucas Bergvall as an Elliot Anderson replacement, but Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi insists he is staying in north London.

Forest could also add a right wing-back, with Dodo at Fiorentina a player of interest.

Dilane Bakwa is set to join Lille on loan, while centre-backs Zach Abbott and Tyler Bindon could also depart on temporary moves amid interest from Watford.

Sports.title: Littler's bid for historic PDC majors sweep suffers blow
Sports.content:
Luke Littler's bid to qualify for the Players Championship Finals, and keep alive his hopes of claiming a historic clean sweep of PDC major titles in 2026, suffered a blow with a quarter-final exit at PC27.

Littler was beaten 6-5 by Jermaine Wattimena in a final-leg decider, with the Dutchman going on to take the title in Leicester, overcoming countryman Kevin Doets 8-6 in the final.

Littler beat Archie Self 6-2, Arno Merk 6-3 and then William O'Connor 6-3 to set up a last-16 tie with Chris Dobey, who he thrashed 6-0, before losing out to eventual champion Wattimena.

Image: Littler has won every PDC major title so far in 2026

The world No 1 has won every major title on the PDC circuit so far in 2026 - the World Championship, Masters, UK Open, Premier League, World Cup of Darts and World Matchplay.

He still needs to win the World Series, World Grand Prix, European Championship, Grand Slam of Darts and Players Championship Finals this season in order to achieve something no-one has ever managed in the sport.

Can Littler still qualify for Players Championship Finals?

The major obstacle standing in the way of a Littler clean sweep is that only the top 64 in the Players Championship Order of Merit make it through to the finals in Minehead in November, with the projected cut-off expected to be over £30,000 in earnings.

The winner of each Players Championship event scoops up £15,000 but Littler was able to secure only £4,000 by reaching the quarter-finals on his season-debut outing.

The 19-year-old opted out of the first 26 events before entering PC27 and 28 in Leicester, meaning he needs to have strong showings in the final seven scheduled floor events to stand a chance of qualifying.

PC28 on Wednesday, also being held at the Mattioli Arena in Leicester, gives him another opportunity to claim a tournament win and boost his finals hopes.

How Wattimena stormed to PC27 title

Wattimena fended off a late fightback Doets to clinch his third PDC ranking title with victory in the Players Championship 27 showpiece on Tuesday.

Sports.title: Manchester United confirm Carlos Baleba signing as midfield spend nears £150m
Sports.content:
Manchester United have completed the signing of the Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in a deal worth up to £70m. The Cameroon international is the third midfielder to join this summer, after Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

Baleba has signed a five-year contract with the option to extend for 12 months after United agreed a £65m deal plus £5m in add-ons and a sell-on with Brighton. It takes the club’s spend on midfielders to about £148m.

Santos and Tielemans have arrived from Chelsea and Aston Villa respectively during a summer when Casemiro left and Manuel Ugarte sustained a serious knee injury.

“It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams,” Baleba said. “Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.

“I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick. His experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.

“The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.”

United made a move to bring in Baleba last summer but cooled their pursuit when Brighton made it clear he was not leaving. Baleba was not at his best last season but that did not put off United, who stepped up their interest in the 22-year-old a week ago.

United’s director of football, Jason Wilcox, said: “Carlos is an elite midfielder with immense potential to develop further. He brings a unique combination of qualities that will really complement our squad.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Two goals, some polish and a rebrand: City flip Sávio for quite the profit
Sports.content:
BRAZILIAN WINGERS UNDER THE HAMMER

We see Manchester City have managed to flip Savinho for quite the profit. Football Daily had previously assumed this sort of wheeler-dealing was restricted to the Dion-Dublin-adjacent property market, or the Harry-Redknapp-infused used car scene, but it seems we were mistaken. We have no idea how City ended up trousering a £44.2m markup on a player who cost £30.8m two seasons ago, and has achieved the square root of eff all since, but they’ve done it. Consider standing stock still and allowing a ball to clank off you and into the net in an FA Cup tie at Newcastle analogous to installing a new bathroom suite and giving the front room a lick of paint, or taking a microfibre cloth and some polish to the crevices of that grimy dashboard. Result! Goal! Ker-ching! That’s 75 million-nil!

Spurs were the mark, and they could end up paying £85m if all the silverware-related add-ons kick in. So £75m it is, then. But that’s still a fair old whack for an attacking player who scored two goals for City in 53 league appearances. The 22-year-old Brazilian plays on the right flank, so will almost certainly take the place of Mikey Moore, who thought his day at Brentford last weekend had gone badly enough, only for his manager Roberto De Zerbi to go out of his way to namecheck him – and him alone, twice – in his post-match deconstruction of a 3-0 fiasco for which pretty much everyone wearing Tottenham’s traditional blue, gold and dayglo pink was culpable.

Upon signing, Savinho announced that he wishes to be known forthwith as Sávio, reverting to the monicker from his time at Girona, where he scored 11 goals and set up 10 others during a loan stint that was a damn sight more successful than his spell at the Etihad. It’s also his actual name, so there is that. Sávio is far from the first of his countrymen to toy with this most personal of brands – Brazil’s greatest-ever player was actually called Manuel Francisco dos Santos, and Pelé was the result of a name change too – and we’re pretty sure he won’t be the last. Spurs meanwhile will simply be hoping they’re getting the Girona version of their new purchase, because otherwise City will have, in more ways than one, properly flipped them off. Omar Marmoush – 16 goals in 62 appearances, brand-new kitchen worktops, shiny hubcaps – next!

RECOMMENDED FOLLOWING

Now on BlueSpace, TikBook, Instachat, all the lesser disgraces.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football. Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough” – a group of influential current and former footballers, including Mikaël Silvestre, Lucy Bronze, Emmanual Petit and David James, have piled more pressure on Gianni Infantino by calling for change at the top of Fifa. However the Cameroon Football Federation’s head-honcho and one-time unimpressed interviewee, Samuel Eto’o, dismissed criticism of Infantino’s leadership. “I don’t think that [he] has done anything wrong,” he honked. “I think the timing of all [the criticism] is because there’s an election coming out.”

double quotation mark Re: the ‘hand of God’ ball’s sale (yesterday’s News, Bits and Bobs, full email edition). I understand Peter Shilton did, in fact, intend to bid but couldn’t get his hand up high enough” – John Myles.

double quotation mark As much as people dislike Chelsea (the football club that is, not the posh area of London, which is quite nice if a bit dull), Xabi Alonso’s wild experiment to attempt to score so many goals that it even offsets Robert Sánchez’s constant Keystone Cops-style performances in goal is going to be wonderfully exciting” – Noble Francis.

Sports.title: Delap heads to Forest for £50m as Chelsea open talks to sell Jackson to Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest have agreed a deal worth £50m to sign Liam Delap from Chelsea, who have also opened talks over selling Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa.

Xabi Alonso has made João Pedro and Danny Welbeck his main strikers this season, leaving his other frontmen to seek opportunities elsewhere. Forest were one of several clubs interested in Delap, who has struggled since joining Chelsea from Ipswich for £30m last summer, and will pay a club record of £45m plus £5m in add-ons for the 23-year-old.

Delap managed only one league goal last season and was hindered by injuries after leaving Ipswich. But the former Manchester City striker was a key target for Forest’s manager, Oliver Glasner, and has a chance to revive his career at the City Ground.

Chelsea are focused on outgoings before the transfer window shuts next Tuesday and are also hoping to sell Jackson, who was on loan at Bayern Munich last season. The Senegal international is valued at £65m and has been earmarked by Villa as a potential replacement for Ollie Watkins, who is expected to join the Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal.

Chelsea are not willing to agree to another loan for Jackson and want his valuation met but Villa are likely to press for a favourable payment schedule to ensure they can afford a permanent deal. Atlético Madrid are also interested in the 25-year-old, who joined Chelsea from Villarreal in 2023. Unai Emery, Villa’s manager, worked with Jackson at Villarreal.

West Ham’s clearout after relegation from the Premier League is expected to continue with El Hadji Malick Diouf joining Brentford for about £35m. The clubs are in discussions over a deal for the left-back and an agreement is likely soon.

Diouf wants to leave and was left out of the squad when Nuno Espírito Santo’s side continued their disappointing start to the Championship season by losing 2-1 at home against Charlton last Saturday.

West Ham signed the Senegal international for £19m from Slavia Prague last year. Brentford have made four signings and are planning to strengthen further.

Nuno, who is understood to be under growing pressure after West Ham’s flat start, has had his hand weakened by a host of players hoping to force their way out.

The Mexico midfielder Edson Álvarez has not been involved in the first two league games and is the subject of interest from Olympiakos and Real Sociedad.

Torino have had a bid rejected for the midfielder Soungoutou Magassa, who is on Crystal Palace’s shortlist. Marseille could sign the French centre-back Jean-Clair Todibo. West Ham have raised funds through the sales of Mateus Fernandes, Crysencio Summerville and Freddie Potts and have loaned Aaron Wan-Bissaka to Aston Villa and Niclas Füllkrug to Werder Bremen.

Sports.title: WSL academy teams to play in third tier after FA approves controversial plan
Sports.content:
Four Women’s Super League ­academy sides will play in the third tier of the ­pyramid from the ­2027-28 ­season after the ­controversial ­proposal was approved by the ­Football ­Association’s board.

The change forms part of what the FA described as a package of reforms to the Women’s National League “designed to strengthen the women’s football pyramid, raise standards across the league, and improve the development pathway for young players”.

Data showed that young English players were getting significantly fewer competitive ­minutes than their counterparts across Europe’s leading leagues, the FA said.

Quick Guide How do I 

WNL clubs will receive central funding for the first time and changes to the loan market will encourage clubs from the top two divisions to loan players to clubs in the third and fourth tiers.

The WSL academy teams will not be eligible for promotion and will be chosen against criteria to be ­developed in the coming months, the FA said. With the third tier split into two geographical regions, it is expected that two academies will be placed in the northern division and two in the southern.

Sue Day, director of women’s ­football at the FA, said:

“For the game to continue moving forward, the FA Women’s National League must evolve alongside the professional game, and we need to create more opportunities for talented young English players to develop in senior football.”

Sports.title: ‘He’s box office’: Gary Lineker admits wanting Roy Keane to join The Rest Is Football
Sports.content:
With an all-conquering podcast empire and a new deal that will make his football punditry show a regular fixture on Netflix, there seems little left for Gary Lineker to wish for.

However, while the former Match of the Day presenter is full of praise for Alan Shearer and Micah Richards – the fellow pundits on his The Rest Is Football show – Lineker has admitted to admiring a combative figure playing for his main rivals.

Asked which of the plethora of football pundits he would want to poach, Lineker admitted that Roy Keane’s brutal delivery and viral rants meant the former Manchester United captain would be his dream signing.

“He’s box office,” Lineker said during an appearance at the Edinburgh TV festival, before joking that, analytically, the Irishman “doesn’t give you that much”.

“He’s bloody good at being Roy Keane,” he said. “I’ve met Roy a few times. He’s really sweet … he just plays a character and he’s good at it. He’s really good at it, and he obviously knows his [stuff]. I was kidding about the analytical thing, a little bit.”

Keane is a member of a podcast team that has emerged as Lineker’s main opposition – Gary Neville’s The Overlap operation, which includes the Stick to Football show. Soon after The Rest Is Football signed up with Netflix, Stick to Football announced a similar deal with Disney.

While the rivalry is good natured, a tongue-in-cheek Lineker couldn’t help but add a slice of football needle, saying Keane “probably would” 

“You’ve got Gary [Neville] and his team, you’ve got Piers Morgan and his team [making the World Cup Uncensored] show, and they’re just trying to copy,” Lineker joked. “They’re trailing in our wake and I wish them all the very best. There is room, particularly in football. There’s a lot of competition.”

The deals bringing football podcasts to the world’s biggest streaming services are a sign of a thirst for sport content. Given the huge expense of live sporting rights, punditry has become a popular option.

The Rest is Football appeared in Netflix’s daily top 10 charts on every day of its 40-day run of daily episodes filmed during the World Cup, and the US company has opted to continue their partnership during the domestic season.

The Rest is Football obtained more than 7m monthly streams for its content alone last season, leading Lineker to joke that Neville’s outfit was “languishing miles behind”.

Lineker was interviewed on stage about his transition from footballer to presenter to media mogul, as the co-founder of successful podcast stable, Goalhanger. During the appearance, he explained why he continued to speak out on political issues, particularly Gaza.

In the last week, the Telegraph criticised him for reposting a video of Tony Greenstein, an anti-Zionist who was cleared last week of inviting support for Hamas. In the video, the activist said: “Zionism is in the tradition of the Nazis who persecuted Jews.”

11:01 Gary Lineker calls for Burnham to introduce wealth tax - The Latest

Lineker said: “I don’t think I speak much about politics, although politics is involved in everything that I speak about.

“I think ultimately you need to live with yourself and if I see things that upset me in humanitarian terms, then I find it quite upsetting, and it triggers me to use a platform that I would never have had before … People can disagree and that’s absolutely fine.”

Sports.title: Post-Pep Premier League era begins with blast of hyper-managed shock and awe | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
There has been something oddly narcotic and moreish about the drip‑drip of fresh Pep Guardiola content either side of the start of the new Premier League season. Eras come and go. Everything dies, baby, that’s a fact. But four‑part Amazon Prime documentaries make angels of us all.

So we have continued to feast on the Pep-at-City visuals: dead jeopardy, reheated beefs, the uplifting team talks of a departed manager to the departed players of a departed team, and moments that often feel far more gripping than the daily churn of what we must, out of habit, call the real world.

The thought occurred watching all this: has the Premier League found its Tupac? Is Pep just going to keep on doing this, dropping new material, fresh hits, posthumous platinum albums? A bald, thin charismatic man who keeps on releasing his lost tapes. We have exactly the thing, sir. Is he even actually dead?

Probably this won’t happen. But a profound absence is still a profound presence at moments like these. The ghosts continue to pull the strings. This weekend was the first of the new Premier League season. More significantly, it was also the first of the post‑Pep era.

And this has been a genuine era, 10 years in the game and an entire tactical culture shift in the making. Unsurprisingly, there was an odd sense of lightness across those nine fixtures on Friday through to Sunday, of old bonds cast aside, even a little giddiness. Suddenly dad isn’t home. The chair by the door is empty. Let’s all just rip it up a bit, shall we?

This relies on a slightly out‑of‑date notion of what Guardiola‑ism became in its later years. But the fact is, something interesting did happen in those Friday‑to‑Sunday games. Think of pure Pep-ball and what are you seeing? Possession. Cold, high‑craft control. This is a coach who famously said: “My desire is to have 100% possession,” after a 5-1 thrashing of Arsenal in Munich during which Thiago Alcântara complete 122 passes.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca acknowledges the fans before City’s opener against Bournemouth. Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty Images

Admittedly, Guardiola was speaking out of frustration that day, talking more about not losing the ball at key moments, possession as defence. But these ideas did have a profound mimetic effect in England. During Guardiola’s decade at Manchester City the team that had the least possession in the Premier League would win, on average, only 30%-35% of games, a figure that fell as low as 28% in 2021‑22 but which had begun to pick up in the last two seasons as even City’s own version of Pep‑ball became more mixed and next‑gen.

But this weekend the opposite thing happened. In six of nine games played from Friday to Sunday one team took significantly more possession while failing to win. Liverpool had 60% possession plus 27 shots but still just scrambled a draw and looked, frankly, pretty wild. Manchester United had 71% possession and were well beaten by Hull. Tottenham had 60 % possession and lost 3-0. Nottingham Forest had 56% and lost. Sunderland had 62%, Crystal Palace 58%, and both lost.

There were three exceptions to this, all outliers in their own way. Manchester City had 66% possession and won at home against Bournemouth, but spent 84 minutes looking like they were losing. Brighton had 73% possession and beat an Aston Villa team that had made a collective decision to play with their eyes closed and their legs on the wrong way round. Arsenal dominated every metric against a promoted Coventry team that looked, frankly, a little spooked by their first sight of that fresh Everest.

So, a tiny sample size. It may mean absolutely nothing. It could get flipped on its head before we hit September. Also, it is important to note that pure possession stats have rarely dictated with any certainty who will win a game. The top teams always tend to have most of the ball, thus skewing the overall stats.

Otherwise, possession has been a far less reliable guide to victory than, say, expected goals, which speaks clearly to the effectiveness of a system. Whereas simply keeping the ball is often a sign of the opposite of good health, of football as a collective anxiety attack, out there playing with your worry beads, tramping a horseshoe shape into the grass while your opponents mass for the decisive blitzkrieg.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

But it wasn’t just the possession numbers that were notable this weekend. The rhythms of the matches were striking. All three Sunday games featured nine or 10 substitutes in the last 40 minutes or so, and a sense of two separate halves, of finishers brought into play, of a broken, episodic tactical to‑and‑fro in response to shifts in the scoreline and the flow. The World Cup also had that pattern. Maybe this is what football is now.

Mainly there was a striking level of targeted physicality, rehearsed blitz-transitions, groups of players running suddenly forward quickly in formation at certain triggering events. Anthony Elanga’s opener for Newcastle captured this best: 12 seconds, two passes, 70 metres covered in a single perfectly straight line, no off‑the‑cuff inventions or what you might call conventional “creativity”, but a perfect moment of planned collective intelligence and breathtaking athleticism.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This was the pattern elsewhere too, games defined by rapid breaks, by powerful players sourced for their ability to win duels and to carry the ball, and a weekend that felt like another ratcheting up in the Premier League’s journey into hyper‑physicality.

Isn’t it a trend? Is this the next stage in the league’s narrow but furiously intense evolution? There are several managers in new jobs who have reputations for the game of sprints, blitz‑ball: most notably Matthias Jaissle at Newcastle and Roberto De Zerbi at what was, on Saturday, the least De Zerbi‑ish of Spurs, a Spurs that seemed to have absorbed only the mouse part – play dead, hide, roll over – of that fast‑breaking cat‑and‑mouse football.

There are two things worth saying about this. This is not a rejection of Guardiolaism and positional play. Keeping the ball was always about preparing for the moments when you don’t have it. Guardiola’s later Manchester City team would often win by direct means.

But pure possession can also be boringly risk-averse, a kind of footballing atrophy where everyone just sits quivering on the touchline like a swarm of beached jellyfish at dusk. The spectacle is more gripping when the emphasis is on those transitions either side of the passing patterns.

More specifically, it is also an interesting development for Pep’s successor at City, Enzo Maresca, Coolio to his Tupac, whose methods are still very much pure Pep origins, based in control of the ball and rigid positionism, like the last soldier still fighting the second world war from inside a bush on Iwo Jima in 1976.

View image in fullscreen Newcastle’s Anthony Elanga celebrates his superb strike against Liverpool. Photograph: Simon Davies/ProSports/Shutterstock

Is Maresca ready for this? Is he even ahead of it? He gave a televised interview at the weekend where he spoke about the tension between control and risk, possession and creativity, and where he defined players being encouraged to run into unexpected positions as “chaos”. On Monday morning there were headlines describing the Premier League weekend in those terms. But this isn’t chaos. We’ve seen chaos. We’ve seen attack ships on fire off the shoulder of Orion, jinking wingers, dogs of war, hitting the space, Lee Chapman, Rod Wallace and Eric Cantona making heavy metal music with two bass guitars and an antique viola. You want chaos. We can give you chaos.

What the Premier League brought at the weekend, the quick breaks, the freedom to attack at selected moments, was more a kind of hyper-managed shock and awe, targeted speed and physicality born out of calculated risk, numbers, data, heavy briefings.

It was also exciting to watch, which is no bad thing in the world’s most tightly contested, space‑averse league. No doubt there will be tightening, a reaction to the reaction, instant counter‑moves and contingency planning. August can also be odd and silly season-ish, the dog days of a World Cup summer. But it did at times feel as if we were in a post‑something moment. If not quite post‑Pep, whose influence will continue to loom, a tactical Machiavelli with plenty of tapes still left in the vault.

Sports.title: ‘Enough is enough’: players pile pressure on under-fire Gianni Infantino to resign
Sports.content:
A group of influential current and former footballers have added to the pressure on Gianni Infantino by calling for change at the top of Fifa, saying “enough is enough” in a statement shared widely across social media.

The intervention is particularly significant given some of those behind its circulation have undertaken ambassadorial activities for Fifa as part of its “Fifa Legends” programme. Among them is the former Manchester United and Arsenal defender Mikaël Silvestre, who also sits on the governing body’s 16-member players’ voice panel designed to assist with anti-racism initiatives.

Others to have shared the statement include the England defender Lucy Bronze, the former England keeper David James and the France 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit. More signatories are expected to follow in a concerted reaction to Infantino’s ill-fated attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup.

“We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” part of the statement read. “Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under Fifa’s current leadership. For too long, we’ve seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football. Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.”

The group called for efforts to “reshape the future of our sport”, adding: “There are good people within Fifa who want to rebuild trust, but a new era requires a structured change: a real, direct say for players and fans in how football is run. Those who step on to the pitch and those who sit in the stands deserve a genuine voice to help reshape football’s future together.”

Infantino has resisted calls to resign and spent Saturday at a youth tournament in the Dominican Republic, attempting to smooth relations with some of the smaller Caribbean member associations on whose support his fate may hinge.

One former player with a different perspective on Infantino is the former Real Madrid, Barcelona and Chelsea striker Samuel Eto’o, who is president of the Cameroonian football federation. In an interview with CNN, Eto’o said Infantino had not committed any missteps and called for the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme to be put back on the table if Infantino is re-elected next March. He said the money from FFE would “reset the balance of power” in football and ensure African countries avoided losing top players to other national teams.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I don’t think that [Infantino] has done anything wrong,” he said. “All of this has happened because there’s an election coming out, that’s all there is.

“I want to see all of my colleagues, all of the presidents, re-reading the project. After president Infantino is re-elected, we will have the strength to ask for this project to be put back on the table for discussion. I remain convinced that, if there is a democratic vote, this project will be adopted because it’s good for the majority.”

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 4: Brighton
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 6th (NB: this is not necessarily Sophie Downey’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 7th

Prospects

A first FA Cup final was a historic moment for Brighton. Despite losing to Manchester City at Wembley, it will have filled Dario Vidosic and his team with the belief that they are on the right track.

It has been a summer of relative stability on the south coast. While there are seven new faces, departures have been limited to four. The arrivals of Lia Wälti and Gabby George bring vast experience and increased defensive acumen to the ranks while the Republic of Ireland’s Emily Murphy and Poland’s Nadia Krezyman are young attacking talents who have started to make a name for themselves.

Brighton’s inconsistency was their downfall last season. They were seriously hampered by the lack of an out-and-out centre-forward after the anterior cruciate ligament injury suffered by the Arsenal loanee and England Euros hero Michelle Agyemang. Kiko Seike finished as their highest scorer in the league with eight and she was their only representative in the Women’s Super League’s top 20 for goals and assists. That problem remains unsolved and will surely be a focus for the remainder of the transfer window.

The conclusion of their season certainly gave Brighton something to build on over the summer. They secured an impressive league victory over City and a draw against Arsenal and will hope to outdo the latter when they host Renée Slegers’s side at Crawley in their opener on 6 September. That on paper is the toughest of Brighton’s opening four fixtures.

Off-field picture

Pinterest has become the first solo sponsor of the women’s team with a four-year partnership. The deal pivots around the concept of ‘matchday style’, bringing to life the way fans show support for their team. Plans continue for the construction of Europe’s first purpose-built women’s football stadium. Located next to the Amex Stadium, the hope is it will open for the start of the 2030-2031 campaign.

The manager

Now entering his third season, Vidosic is the second-longest serving manager in the WSL, a period that has brought much-needed stability to the club and allowed the Croatian-born Australian time to fully implement his aggressive pressing and possession-based style. He has been on a journey, developing an out-of-possession style to help his team deal with some of the bigger clubs in the WSL The 39-year-old has never hidden from his desire to bring silverware to Brighton and last season’s FA Cup final will have given him a taste of the steps required to realise that ambition.

Star signing

The acquisition of Wälti remains one of the biggest coups of the summer. The 33-year-old Switzerland captain returns to England after a year in Italy with Juventus, bringing with her a wealth of experienceand, from her seven years with Arsenal, a WSL title and a Champions League winners’ medal. Wälti’s technical ability is second-to-none, as is a level of intelligence that allows her to dictate play from the middle of the park. She leads by example and guided Switzerland to the quarter-finals at Euro 2025. If Wälti can stay injury-free, she could play a significant role this season.

View image in fullscreen Lia Wälti should bring quality and know-how to Brighton. Photograph: Neil Holmes/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

Stat attack

Brighton had a finishing problem in 2025-26. Not in terms of hitting the target – no other side had as strong a shot accuracy – but only three teams converted a lower proportion of their on-target efforts. If the Seagulls can fire towards the corners of the goal rather than close to the goalkeeper, they could fly this season.

Set for a breakthrough

Sophie Peskett has already made history when in 2021, aged 18, she became Ipswich’s first professional player. The winger spent the best part of seven years at Ipswich, making 127 appearances and helping them earn promotion to the WSL 2 twice. Now 23, it would have been a big decision for her to leave, but Brighton seems like a sensible next step. A nifty player with an eye for goal, Peskett will prove useful to Brighton’s attacking output.

What they say …

“Brighton is not a team that has to hide. In the last couple of years, they’ve been able to hurt the big teams in many moments, and they reached the FA Cup final last season as well. We’re not going to be favourites in every single game, but that’s a nice position to be in.” – Lia Wälti

Where are they playing their home games?

Brighton will continue to play most of their home games at Crawley’s Broadfield Stadium although four of their six opening home fixtures will be at the Amex. The club have added an Amex 4-Match Pack to their ticketing options, priced at £45 for adults. The club have also launched ‘Built For Her’, their dedicated women’s football membership option that offers a bundle of exclusive perks as they look to build their fanbase before the stadium move.

Sports.title: Chelsea's summer clear-out continues as Blues close in on agreeing staggering £115MILLION double sale of strikers Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson
Sports.content:
Chelsea's summer clear-out continues as Blues close in on agreeing staggering £115MILLION double sale of strikers Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Chelsea have agreed a staggering £50million sale Liam Delap to Nottingham Forest.

Delap is now in line to leave Stamford Bridge after only a single season, with the Blues having triggered his £30m release clause at Ipswich Town last summer.

He scored one Premier League goal in 28 games in 2025-26, and two in 41 in all competitions.

Delap was missing from the Chelsea squad which defeated Fulham 3-2 in their first Premier League fixture of the season.

The 23-year-old had been training separately to Xabi Alonso’s main group at their Cobham base after being made available for sale, along with Nicolas Jackson.

Jackson is also closing in on a £65m switch to Aston Villa. That would see Chelsea secure their asking price for the 25-year-old Senegalese.

Chelsea have agreed a £50million fee with Nottingham Forest to sell them Liam Delap

Nicolas Jackson is also nearing a £65million move to Aston Villa from Chelsea

The Chelsea star is understood to be keen on a reunion with former boss Unai Emery

They had been seeking at least £50m for Delap. It is believed Forest’s agreement involves £45m plus £5m in add-ons.

It represents a remarkable profit secured by Chelsea after a disappointing campaign for Delap, whose No 9 shirt was handed to Joao Pedro before this current season started.

Delap had been keen to stay at Chelsea and prove himself, but he became surplus this summer.

With Joao Pedro untouchable at the front of Chelsea's attack, they also signed Danny Welbeck from Brighton and have Emmanuel Emegha. Jackson and Marc Guiu are in line to leave.

Sports.title: Stars hit the red carpet at the PFA Awards: Bruno Fernandes is joined by WAG as Declan Rice leads FIVE Arsenal players in attendance with football world descending on Manchester for bash
Sports.content:
Stars hit the red carpet at the PFA Awards: Bruno Fernandes is joined by WAG as Declan Rice leads FIVE Arsenal players in attendance with football world descending on Manchester for bash

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A plethora of key figures within English football have all descended upon Manchester ahead of Tuesday night's Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) Awards.

The annual ceremony is taking place this year at the Opera House Theatre.

Among those in attendance sees representation from several Premier League teams.

Champions Arsenal are represented by a key quintet of David Raya, Jurrien Timber, Gabriel Magalhaes, William Saliba and Declan Rice. Those five will hope to be involved in at least the PFA Team of the Year, while potentially collecting the prize for PFA Player of the Year.

Arsenal were in a title pursuit with Manchester City all of last season and beat them in the Community Shield two Sundays ago.

That quintet will cross paths with City trio Antoine Semenyo, Rayan Cherki and Nico O'Reilly who are also there.

Arsenal stars David Raya, Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber, Gabriel Magalhaes and William Saliba (left to right) were on the red carpet ahead of the PFA Awards in Manchester on Tuesday night

Manchester City were represented at the bash by Antoine Semenyo (centre) and Rayan Cherki

Semenyo enjoyed a prolific season at Bournemouth and City last term, while O'Reilly had a breakout campaign which saw him end it as part of England head coach Thomas Tuchel's - who is also attending - World Cup squad which reached the semi-finals.

Aged just 21, the City academy graduate is the favourite to win PFA Young Player of the Year.

City's bitter rivals Manchester United are represented by head coach Michael Carrick, CEO Omar Berrada and Bruno Fernandes.

The pair have had a busy day following the £70million transfer completion of Carlos Baleba from Brighton and Hove Albion.

Baleba will add some much-needed dynamism to United's midfield and will play behind captain Fernandes - who is another leading contender for the PFA Player of the Year award after a fantastic 2025-26 where he broke the Premier League assists record for a single season with 21.

In May, he won the Football Writers' Association's men's Footballer of the Year award and was named Premier League player of the season, meaning it could be a clean sweep of accolades if he's victorious come 9pm.

Liverpool icon Kenny Dalglish also donned the red carpet alongside his wife Marina.

Arsenal are also well represented in the women's game in Manchester with Alessia Russo, Mariona Caldentey, Emily Fox and Olivia Smith representing the Gunners too.

Nico O'Reilly (left) could win PFA Young Player, in front of England boss Thomas Tuchel there

Bruno Fernandes registered a record-breaking 21 assists in the Premier League last season

Michael Carrick (left) and Omar Berrada are among those representing Manchester United

Liverpool legend Kenny Dalglish smiles for the cameras alongside his wife Marina

Arsenal Women's Olivia Smith, Mariona Caldentey, Alessia Russo, and Emily Fox (left-right) attended Tuesday's event at the Manchester Opera Theatre

Former Lionesses Karen Carney, Eni Aluko, Jordan Nobbs and Toni Duggan are also in the crowd for Tuesday night's showpiece.

In terms of former male footballers the likes of Mikael Silvestre, Sebastian Bassong, Ashley Young, Asmir Begovic, Kolo Toure are also present.

Ex-Manchester United and Arsenal defender Silvestre hit the headlines on Monday after calling out FIFA president Gianni Infantino, telling him to stand down.

Silvestre, who is part of FIFA's Players' Voice Panel, took to X to demand change, writing: 'Enough is enough!'

The post, which went on to call for structural change within FIFA, was shared by France 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit as well as Lioness Lucy Bronze.

Infantino is also facing calls to quit from his UEFA counterpart Aleksander Ceferin in the wake of a hugely controversial plan to sell stakes in a company to run the World Cup to private investors.

And players have now begun to speak out against the 56-year-old, with Monday's widely shared statement evidential of those who 'share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world'.

Karen Carney (left) and Mikael Silvestre are among the ex-footballers at Tuesday's ceremony

It added: 'Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under FIFA's current leadership.

'For too long we've seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

'Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership's ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football.'

Silvestre's interjection is significant given it effectively comes from within the FIFA fold, with the Players' Voice Panel a 16-strong group formed by the global governing body to monitor and advise on initiatives to tackle racism.

The statement continued: 'Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.

'We call on all stakeholders to step forward and help reshape the future of our sport.'
